accepted.s: The Green Credit Programme was introduced in October 2023 under which of the following legal provisions?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
accepted.x: The Green Credit Programme was introduced in October 2023 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its correct parent legislation.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: Which of the following is the administrator of the Green Credit Programme?
o: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, New Delhi
Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, Dehradun
accepted.x: The Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE), Dehradun, administers the Green Credit Programme.
accepted.tq: Use the administrator-location pair to distinguish neighbouring environmental institutions.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT covered as an activity under the Green Credit Programme?
accepted.x: The programme covers activities such as tree planting, water management, sustainable agriculture, waste management, air-pollution reduction, mangroves, ecomark and sustainable buildings. Deep-sea mineral extraction is not listed.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the programme’s stated activity list.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Green Credit Programme:
1. It is a market-based incentive mechanism.
2. It is intended only for compulsory environmental actions.
3. Afforestation credits under it can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The programme is a market-based incentive for voluntary environmental actions, so statement 2 is false. Afforestation under the programme can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.
accepted.tq: Identify the false extreme word ‘only’ and retain the two supported statements.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme of India combines which of the following mechanisms?
o: A compliance mechanism and an offset mechanism
A voluntary mechanism and an import mechanism
A taxation mechanism and a subsidy mechanism
A conservation mechanism and a litigation mechanism
accepted.x: The Indian Carbon Market combines a compliance mechanism for energy-intensive sectors with an offset mechanism for voluntary projects in ten sectors.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two complementary designs of the carbon market.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: Under the compliance mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, an obligated entity that performs better than its notified GHG Emission Intensity target:
o: Must purchase additional Carbon Credit Certificates
Receives a Carbon Credit Certificate that can be traded
Receives a direct compensation from the Union Budget
Is exempted from all environmental regulations
accepted.x: Entities that beat their notified GHG Emission Intensity targets earn tradeable Carbon Credit Certificates. Entities that miss their targets must buy certificates.
accepted.tq: Apply the compliance rule to the entity’s performance against its target.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the offset mechanism under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
o: It applies only to obligated aluminium and cement units.
It covers voluntary projects in ten sectors using approved methodologies.
It permits offsets without any approved methodology.
It covers compulsory projects in all agricultural districts.
accepted.x: The offset mechanism covers voluntary projects in ten sectors, including agriculture and waste, and uses approved methodologies.
accepted.tq: Separate the voluntary offset design from the mandatory compliance design.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was notified in June 2023 under Section 14AA of the:
o: Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022
accepted.x: The scheme was notified in June 2023 under Section 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022.
accepted.tq: Check the exact section-and-statute combination.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was designed to contribute to which intensity-reduction target?
accepted.x: The scheme was designed to meet the 45 percent intensity target.
accepted.tq: Use the nearby percentage figures as a numerical discrimination test.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: Who administers the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education under the Ministry of Environment
Central Pollution Control Board under the Ministry of Coal
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power
accepted.x: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, under the Ministry of Power, administers the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method for institutional responsibility.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Carbon Market:
1. The compliance mechanism assigns GHG Emission Intensity targets to obligated entities.
2. Entities missing their targets are required to buy Carbon Credit Certificates.
3. The offset mechanism is limited to projects in ten sectors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: compliance entities receive intensity targets, underperforming entities buy certificates, and the offset mechanism covers voluntary projects in ten sectors.
accepted.tq: Test the complete compliance-versus-offset comparison.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: The GHG Emission Intensity targets notified in October 2025 initially covered which group of sectors?
o: Aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp and paper
accepted.x: The October 2025 targets covered aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp and paper.
accepted.tq: Match the notification with its exact sectoral coverage.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: The October 2025 GHG Emission Intensity notification covered how many obligated entities?
accepted.x: The notification covered 282 obligated entities.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact entity count from nearby values.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the current scale of the Indian carbon market as stated?
o: Ten sectors, about 282 industries and about 477 Mt CO2e
Four sectors, about 490 industries and about 282 Mt CO2e
Seven sectors, about 282 industries and about 490 Mt CO2e
Seven sectors, about 490 industries and about 477 Mt CO2e
accepted.x: The market covers seven sectors, approximately 490 industries and about 477 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent.
accepted.tq: Keep the sector, industry and emissions figures aligned in the same order.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: According to the stated comparison, which group of jurisdictions covers more sectors or entities through carbon markets than India?
o: China, the European Union and South Korea
accepted.x: Only China, the European Union and South Korea were stated to cover more than India in this comparison.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise comparative group rather than a generally prominent climate actor.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme demonstrated the effectiveness of market-based regulation by reducing emissions of:
accepted.x: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme reduced particulate-matter emissions by 20–30 percent.
accepted.tq: Link the scheme with the pollutant and the reduction range.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project in Meghalaya is significant because it is India’s first:
o: Compensatory-afforestation project under the Green Credit Programme
accepted.x: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project is India’s first Plan Vivo-certified REDD+ project.
accepted.tq: Use the certification body as the decisive identifier.
accepted.sec: Green Credit Programme and carbon market

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Coalition)
A. Global Biofuels Alliance
B. LeadIT
C. Mission Innovation
D. International Big Cat Alliance

List-II (Origin or launch)
1. COP21, Paris, 2015
2. India’s G20 Presidency, 2023
3. Mysuru, April 2023

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched during India’s G20 Presidency; LeadIT was set up by India and Sweden in 2019; Mission Innovation began at COP21 in 2015; and the Big Cat Alliance was launched at Mysuru in April 2023.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure launch locations and years, then eliminate mismatched codes.
accepted.sec: India-led climate coalitions - GBA, LeadIT, Mission Innovation, Big Cat Alliance

accepted.s: LeadIT primarily works towards the low-carbon transition of which sectors?
accepted.x: LeadIT focuses particularly on low-carbon transitions in the steel and cement sectors and aligns heavy industry with the Paris goals.
accepted.tq: Match the coalition with its specialised industrial focus.
accepted.sec: India-led climate coalitions - GBA, LeadIT, Mission Innovation, Big Cat Alliance

accepted.s: LeadIT was launched by India and Sweden at the:
accepted.x: LeadIT was launched by India and Sweden at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founding event from the later summit co-chairing event.
accepted.sec: India-led climate coalitions - GBA, LeadIT, Mission Innovation, Big Cat Alliance

accepted.s: At COP29 in Baku in November 2024, India’s Minister of State Kirti Vardhan Singh co-chaired the LeadIT Summit with:
accepted.x: Kirti Vardhan Singh co-chaired the LeadIT Summit with Sweden’s Romina Pourmokhtari at COP29 in Baku.
accepted.tq: Apply the person-event-country association carefully.
accepted.sec: India-led climate coalitions - GBA, LeadIT, Mission Innovation, Big Cat Alliance

accepted.s: Mission Innovation was launched at which of the following events?
accepted.x: Mission Innovation was launched at COP21 in Paris in 2015, and India is a founding member.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among COP numbers, locations and years.
accepted.sec: India-led climate coalitions - GBA, LeadIT, Mission Innovation, Big Cat Alliance

accepted.s: The International Big Cat Alliance covers how many big-cat species?
accepted.x: The International Big Cat Alliance covers seven big cats.
accepted.tq: Test the exact numerical scope of the alliance.
accepted.sec: India-led climate coalitions - GBA, LeadIT, Mission Innovation, Big Cat Alliance

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s negotiating stance on climate change:
1. India invokes equity and climate justice.
2. India supports the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities.
3. NDC 3.0 is framed around continuity and incremental advance within India’s equitable share.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements describe India’s stated negotiating position: equity, climate justice, CBDR-RC, and continuity with incremental advance within its equitable share.
accepted.tq: Combine the three linked principles and policy formulations in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: India's negotiating stance - climate justice, per-capita emissions, finance, NDC 2035

accepted.s: Global climate finance reached approximately what amount in 2023, according to the stated assessment?
accepted.x: Global climate finance reached approximately USD 1.9 trillion in 2023.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among adjacent trillion-dollar figures.
accepted.sec: India's negotiating stance - climate justice, per-capita emissions, finance, NDC 2035

accepted.s: Developing countries other than China received approximately what share of global climate finance in 2023?
accepted.x: Developing countries other than China received only about 15 percent of global climate finance in 2023.
accepted.tq: Test the comparative share rather than the total finance figure.
accepted.sec: India's negotiating stance - climate justice, per-capita emissions, finance, NDC 2035

accepted.s: India relies mainly on domestic resources for climate finance, with approximately what share coming from domestic resources?
accepted.x: India relies mainly on domestic resources, which account for approximately 83 percent of its climate finance.
accepted.tq: Use the percentage-range trap to identify the precise domestic-finance share.
accepted.sec: India's negotiating stance - climate justice, per-capita emissions, finance, NDC 2035

accepted.s: According to India’s first Biennial Transparency Report, what proportion of emissions in 2022 came from industry?
accepted.x: The first Biennial Transparency Report indicated that over 20 percent of emissions in 2022 came from industry.
accepted.tq: Use the broad sectoral share before testing its internal components.
accepted.sec: India's negotiating stance - climate justice, per-capita emissions, finance, NDC 2035

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the industrial-emissions breakdown reported for 2022?
o: 20 percent from fuel use in manufacturing and construction, and 13 percent from industrial processes
13 percent from fuel use in manufacturing and construction, and 9 percent from industrial processes
13 percent from industrial processes, and 9 percent from agriculture
9 percent from fuel use in manufacturing and construction, and 13 percent from industrial processes
accepted.x: The reported breakdown was 13 percent from fuel use in manufacturing and construction and 9 percent from industrial processes, together exceeding 20 percent.
accepted.tq: Preserve the correct order of the two component percentages and sectors.
accepted.sec: India's negotiating stance - climate justice, per-capita emissions, finance, NDC 2035

accepted.s: India’s target for additional carbon dioxide equivalent sequestration through its carbon sink by 2030 is:
accepted.x: India’s 2030 carbon-sink target is 2.5–3.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent.
accepted.tq: Test the target range against neighbouring ranges.
accepted.sec: Carbon sink target - forest and tree cover, Green India Mission, trees outside forests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: How much carbon sink had been added so far against India’s 2030 target, according to the stated 2026 assessment?
accepted.x: Approximately 2.29 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent had been added so far. The earlier official estimate for 2005–2019 was 1.97 billion tonnes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the latest progress figure from the earlier baseline estimate.
accepted.sec: Carbon sink target - forest and tree cover, Green India Mission, trees outside forests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The official estimate of India’s carbon sink addition for the period 2005–2019 was:
accepted.x: The official estimate for carbon sink addition during 2005–2019 was 1.97 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent.
accepted.tq: Separate the historical estimate from the later cumulative progress figure.
accepted.sec: Carbon sink target - forest and tree cover, Green India Mission, trees outside forests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Forest and tree cover constituted approximately what proportion of India’s geographical area in 2021?
accepted.x: Forest and tree cover accounted for approximately 24.6 percent of India’s geographical area in 2021.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the exact percentage using the decimal figure.
accepted.sec: Carbon sink target - forest and tree cover, Green India Mission, trees outside forests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Green India Mission covers which of the following areas and interventions?
o: Forest cover on 2.5 Mha and mangroves on another 3 Mha
Forest cover on 10 Mha without any quality-improvement component
Quality improvement on 5 Mha and urban plantations on another 10 Mha
Forest cover on 5 Mha and quality improvement on another 5 Mha
accepted.x: The Green India Mission covers forest cover on 5 million hectares and quality improvement on another 5 million hectares.
accepted.tq: Check both the area and the intervention rather than matching only one figure.
accepted.sec: Carbon sink target - forest and tree cover, Green India Mission, trees outside forests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What happened to the original Green India Mission sequestration goal of 50–60 Mt per year?
o: It was replaced by a 2035 industrial-emissions target.
It was folded into the 2030 carbon-sink target.
It was converted into a target exclusively for mangroves.
accepted.x: The original 2020 sequestration goal of 50–60 million tonnes per year is now folded into the 2030 carbon-sink target.
accepted.tq: Trace the relationship between the earlier mission goal and the later national target.
accepted.sec: Carbon sink target - forest and tree cover, Green India Mission, trees outside forests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the stated environmental initiative?
o: MISHTI — more than two billion plants in 16 months
Community campaign — mangroves over 540 square kilometres
Green India Mission — launched exclusively in 2024
accepted.x: Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam was a supporting drive launched in 2024. The community campaign involved over two billion plants in 16 months, while MISHTI covered mangroves over 540 square kilometres.

o: Two hundred million plants in 16 months
accepted.x: The community campaign involved more than two billion plants in 16 months.
accepted.tq: Combine the correct magnitude with the correct time period.

accepted.x: MISHTI was associated with mangrove coverage of more than 540 square kilometres.
